decisions.summary: Stockline's price rose to 0.03, which leaves a 0.02 margin per check and still clears the 0.01 minimum. Ridgeline is cheaper at 0.02 with a 0.03 margin, but 6 of its last 20 tries were unavailable, so I kept the current policy on Stockline (cap 0.03, no cache) for reliable fresh data. No purchases made and no changes to the buy policy.

Packwise Starter is ending and Pro costs 45.00 EUR, above the 30.00 EUR card limit. I asked the CFO to raise the per-purchase card limit to 45.00 (P-0001, awaiting Face ID) and notified Treasury. Buy policy unchanged (Stockline, cap 0.03, no cache). I will buy packwise-pro on the Airwallex card once the raise is approved.

No action: no agent is blocked, the licence invoice INV-2026-1043 is already paid per the ledger, and the 1.31 in net earnings is far less than the other agents may still spend, so a sweep now would move little or nothing. The Packwise card-limit request P-0001 waits for the CFO's Face ID.

Ran settle_dispute on D-f2d71f9a. Refunded nothing. Escalated orders #11–#16 to the CFO as P-0002 with advice to deny, because on-chain evidence shows Summit's own mandate key signed and paid for them.

Planned P-0003 for Stockline invoice SLL-2026-11 (EUR 240.00, due 2026-11-15): SWIFT, fee at most 20.00, converting only the EUR 160.00 shortfall for USD 180.29. It now waits for the CFO's Face ID. No sweep, because 1.31 is less than the other mandates may still spend, and no rebalance, because no agent is blocked.

I did nothing this time. Alpenweg Outdoor paid 1230.00 EUR against NW-R-201, which is 10.00 EUR short, so the payment is in suspense waiting for the CFO. The 10.00 EUR balance stays open and the customer is being asked for it. That decision belongs to the CFO, not me. The Stockline invoice SLL-2026-11 already waits for the CFO's approval as P-0003. The CFO should know that P-0003 was planned before this payment arrived and converts only a 160.00 EUR shortfall, for USD 180.29.
